                    ### Question
                    A 37-year-old man presents a picture of arthritis of the metacarpophalangeal of both hands and a right pleuritis. On examination, bilateral malar erythema was observed. Positive antinuclear antibodies are detected (titre 1/640), with native anti-DNA antibodies also positive; Anti-Sm negative. What would be the initial treatment of choice for this patient?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Glucocorticoids at high doses.
opb. Glucocorticoids and mycophenolate.
opc. Non-steroidal and antimalarial anti-inflammatories.
opd. The picture will probably be self-limiting and does not require treatment.

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The clinical presentation of arthritis, pleuritis, and bilateral malar erythema, along with positive antinuclear antibodies (ANA) and anti-DNA antibodies, strongly supports a diagnosis of Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE). Standard medical consensus for initial treatment of mild to moderate SLE, which includes symptoms like arthritis and pleuritis, typically involves the use of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) and antimalarials such as hydroxychloroquine. This approach helps manage inflammation and prevent disease flares. The retrieved evidence paths confirm the association of SLE with positive ANA and anti-DNA antibodies, supporting the diagnosis. High-dose glucocorticoids or additional immunosuppressants like mycophenolate are generally reserved for more severe manifestations of SLE, which are not indicated in this case. Therefore, the most appropriate initial treatment for this patient is NSAIDs and antimalarials.
